item.title: ‘This is not about politics. This is about people’: UN warns of impact of deadly drone strikes in Sudan
item.description: Intensifying drone attacks on civilian infrastructure across Sudan are disrupting electricity, water and fuel supplies, putting lives at risk and hampering the delivery of humanitarian aid, the UN’s top official in the country has warned.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World News in Brief: Children killed in Myanmar strike, new violence flares in Mozambique, an Internet affordability milestone
item.description: A school in Myanmar has been hit in an airstrike, with three children reported killed and five others injured, according to UN Children’s Fund UNICEF.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Married off at 14: In Yemen’s war, women and girls suffer ‘devastating consequences’
item.description: Safa is 14. Her mother died earlier this year. She has no brothers or sisters. And a few weeks ago, as the crisis took hold, her father married her to an elderly man, afraid that if he were killed in the hostilities, no one would be left to protect her.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Haiti gang leader seeks UN talks as El Salvador sends 2,000 troops to hunt for missing soldiers
item.description: A Haitian gang leader wanted by the United States has asked the UN to mediate, as El Salvador sends more than 2,000 troops into the country to search for four of its soldiers who went missing after a gang ambush.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Gender equality pays off for business – so why are companies pulling back?
item.description: Gender equality and diversity are good for business – but while increasing numbers of women are reaching top spots in the corporate world, more initiatives are needed to keep momentum going.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Air raid alerts and attacks on schools: the devastating face of education in Ukraine
item.description: Ukraine has sustained almost 2,000 attacks on education since the full-scale Russian invasion in 2022, with some 270 this year alone, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) said on Tuesday, a day after a strike at a school being used to distribute aid.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World News in Brief: healthcare crisis in Yemen’s Taiz and Afghanistan, Western Sahara mission's phased closure
item.description: The humanitarian crisis in Yemen is worsening, particularly in the southwestern city of Taiz, which is being encircled by paramilitary Iran-backed Houthi forces.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Ukraine: WFP provides hot meals to Oleshky evacuees as UN pushes to restore power before winter
item.description: The UN World Food Programme (WFP) is providing emergency food assistance to more than 400 people who were able to leave the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, in Ukraine’s Kherson region, during a brief local ceasefire.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Ethiopia: Violence in the north is pushing health system to the brink, WHO chief warns
item.description: The head of the World Health Organization (WHO) called on Monday for greater protection for civilians caught in conflict in northern Ethiopia following deadly drone strikes this past weekend.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Six in seven journalist murders go unpunished, UNESCO reports
item.description: Global impunity for journalist killings has risen for the first time in more than a decade, while the growing use of drones is an emerging threat for reporters in conflict zones, according to the latest report from UN cultural organization UNESCO.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories
